notes: Source of truth for Parquet reader/codec compatibility.

The Results table and fallback section of docs/compatibility-matrix.md are rendered from this file by scripts/render_compat_matrix.py. Everything else in that document is hand-written and is NOT generated -- in particular the four PASS criteria and their pinned expected values.

Tri-state on purpose: true = PASS, false = FAIL, null (or key absent) = not tested yet. Never write false to mean 'unknown'; that would render as FAIL and make the gate look decided on data that does not exist.
Only add a true/false after a real run on real infrastructure. An unpopulated row is the honest state and is what keeps the hard gate closed.

fallback_notes: It is the most broadly supported Parquet codec. If ZSTD fails the matrix, the `gzip-6` arm is already measured and available as the compatible candidate -- at roughly half Snappy's decode throughput (0.40-0.56x, Iteration 1), so the fallback is a real cost, not a free swap.
Snappy and ZSTD files can coexist within the same table: Parquet records the codec per column chunk, so a transition window needs no flag day.
Rollback = rewrite affected partitions with `compression=snappy`. Cost is proportional to the partitions already converted, which argues for converting newest partitions first and oldest last.
